matching_bullets: A maximum-severity flaw in an agent-orchestration harness left 233 privileged tools reachable over HTTP with no password at all
verifications.reason: Covered by orchestration-ness carried inside a security bullet — the same structure the July 29 audit accepted for MDASH, so this is continuity rather than a new latitude. Ruflo is described in the bullet's own words as an open-source multi-agent orchestration platform, which is the rubric's opening clause verbatim ('any agent / workflow / pipeline orchestration platform'), and the label is not the whole of it. The bullet documents the orchestration architecture in detail: a Model Context Protocol bridge implemented as an Express.js server that brokers every tool invocation across agent workflows, exposing 233 high-privilege tools spanning shell command execution, database operations, agent management and memory storage, with agent-swarm spawning and an AgentDB learning store whose poisoned patterns taint the outputs served to every other user of that deployment. Noma's own framing is that the bridge is the platform's central nervous system controlling all tool calls and agent actions, not an auxiliary debug interface. And there is a dated state change in that architecture: maintainer Reuven Cohen shipped version 3.16.3 within 24 hours of the June 30 responsible disclosure, binding the bridge to loopback, requiring a bearer token, gating terminal execution behind explicit opt-in, enabling MongoDB authentication and tightening container and cross-origin controls. Nothing from n8n, LangFlow, Flowise, Temporal, Inngest, Prefect, Restate, Dust.tt, Activepieces or AutoGen Studio; the AGNTCon and MCPCon description of agent infrastructure and production-agent observability is event-ness carried by the events bullet, not an orchestration state change.

News-driven-only topic per the coverage rules, and no trigger fired: the literal string 'Multica' appears in no category, body or citation, and nothing today concerns serving or switching between several local model profiles on one machine. Considered and rejected three near misses. Pull request 7289's size-detection fix reads one model's parameter count from its path — Qwen3.5-35B-A3B had been matched on the active-expert count and read as a 3-billion-parameter model — which is single-model identification, not a profile set a user selects between. Pull request 7645's Vulkan path is backend capability selection, choosing one working path rather than maintaining several concurrently. And Ruflo's 233 tools and spawned agent swarms are tool and agent multiplicity, not model-profile multiplicity; the Unit 42 operator's evaluation across Qwen, GLM, Kimi and MiniMax is a one-time selection decision, not a multi-profile runtime.

verifications.reason: Borderline for the third day running and scored the same way as July 28 and July 29 for continuity, though the substance is thinner than either of those. No inference engine or serving stack is the subject of anything today: nothing from vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, LMDeploy, LiteLLM, RouteLLM, BentoML, Triton, Aphrodite or Ollama serving, and no engine shipped a release, a benchmark or a capability of its own. What keeps this off a flat uncovered is that pull request 7289 changes the serving contract directly, and this row names llama.cpp serving explicitly. A missing reasoning_content field on the ChatMessage model meant Pydantic dropped reasoning silently before the request ever reached the inference server, losing reasoning content between turns in multi-turn Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 conversations; the fix adds the field, teaches truncation to clip reasoning content when the context overflows, and emits an empty content field on reasoning-only assistant turns specifically for llama.cpp compatibility, with 12,583 backend tests passing against a single pre-existing failure and 32 on the frontend. Context-overflow handling and wire-format compatibility with a serving runtime are serving-runtime concerns, but the shipping party is a fine-tuning toolkit's client layer rather than the engine, which is the same one-layer-removed problem flagged on July 29. The vLLM Conference hosted by Inferact and co-located on the Ray Summit pass is event-ness carried by the events bullet.

Five open-weight families are named and all five appear as usage rather than as releases, which is precisely the ground on which the July 29 audit rejected GLM-5.2: the Unit 42 operator evaluated Qwen, GLM, Kimi and MiniMax and ran the campaign itself on DeepSeek, a model-selection decision inside a security story, with the contrast being that OpenAI's safety systems refused the requests and disabled a linked account. verifications.reason: MANDATORY constant-coverage topic, and covered by the unslothai/unsloth repository itself with first-party, dated, individually cited evidence. The bullet does not over-claim, which is what makes the covered verdict defensible: its opening clause states that v0.1.51-beta was tagged the previous afternoon and the 2026.7.6 wheel already published, that no new release tag appeared on Thursday, July 30, and that the day's work went straight into main instead. What is fresh is merge activity on main dated to today, and a merge to main is a real repository state change — this row is 'Local LLM Optimization, Fine-tuning', not 'Unsloth releases', and nothing in the rubric conditions coverage on a version tag or a PyPI artefact. The three pull requests are disjoint from July 29's 7621 / 7619 / 7616 rather than a restatement of them, and each carries its own URL and its own test evidence. Pull request 7289 adds the reasoning_content field the ChatMessage model was missing, so multi-turn Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 conversations stop losing reasoning to a silent Pydantic drop, and replaces size extraction with an anchored pattern scanning path segments from the right, correcting a read of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B as a 3-billion-parameter model that had been switching reasoning off on the larger models outright — 12,583 backend tests passing against one pre-existing failure, 32 on the frontend. Pull request 7631 closes a genuinely destructive default: uninstall.sh and uninstall.ps1 ignored their arguments entirely, so a --help flag or a mistyped option uninstalled the product, and the shell script could partially execute on a truncated curl-to-shell stream; the uninstallers now print usage and remove nothing on a help flag, name the offending argument and exit non-zero on an unknown one, and remove nothing on truncated input, across 25 shell and 39 PowerShell argument tests plus 82 more on shared icons and pipe safety. Pull request 7645 routes six explicit Vulkan setup failures through the failure helpers rather than bare exits so the error surfaces in Studio desktop, with 26 shell installer test files clean and 1,387 Python tests passing. Verdict covered, alignment consistent: the topic was searched, the search produced real dated state change, and the bullet is honest about what did not ship.

Agent hijack, tool-call abuse and MCP exposure: Noma Labs disclosed CVE-2026-59726, named RufRoot, at the maximum CVSS score of 10.0, in which Ruflo's Model Context Protocol bridge exposed POST /mcp with no authentication while the shipped docker-compose configuration bound port 3001 to 0.0.0.0, publishing 233 high-privilege tools to anyone who could reach the port; a single unauthenticated request to the terminal-execution tool runs commands in the container, from which an attacker reads stored user conversations, lifts environment variables holding model API keys, reaches an unauthenticated MongoDB instance, and spawns agent swarms billed to the victim's own keys. Offensive agentic AI: Unit 42's reconstruction of the knaithe campaign, an autonomous offensive operator built on DeepSeek and the Hermes Agent framework, driven from Telegram, with the autonomous-versus-manual split as the finding and OpenAI's refusal-and-account-disablement as the provider-side control that held.
